claims.text: IT PRINTS THE REQUIREMENT AS A NUMBER, IN TWO TABLES. Table 2, 'Negative Energy Required for Warp Bubble (Larger Negative Energy)', and Table 3 after the reduction the paper argues for. At 0.01c: -3.03 x 10^46 J and -1.00 x 10^38 J. At 0.5c: -7.59 x 10^49 J and -2.50 x 10^41 J. AT LIGHT SPEED: -3.03 x 10^50 J and -1.00 x 10^42 J. At twice light speed: -1.21 x 10^51 J and -4.00 x 10^42 J. The document states that on its model 'energy requirements are reduced immensely when compared to the calculations of Lobo and Visser' and that 'All calculations are order-of-magnitude'.

claims.text: ITS OWN SUMMARY, VERBATIM, and what it claims is a possibility and not a result: 'The idea that a sufficiently advanced technology may interact with, and acquire direct control over, the higher dimensions is a tantalizing possibility, and one that is most certainly worthy of deeper investigation. Control of this higher dimensional space may be a source of technological control over the dark energy density and could ultimately play a role in the development of exotic propulsion technologies; specifically, a warp drive. Of course, this may not be actualized until many years in the future...' Its closing sentence: '...if we may make predictions based on the innovative history of scientific pioneers of the past, then it seems entirely possible that the creative minds of the future may indeed find ways to accomplish what, to us, may seem like magic.'

Classical and Quantum Gravity, vol. 11, 1994, pp. L73-L77.' Its introduction states that 'a 1994 paper by Miguel Alcubierre placed the idea on a more solid theoretical footing'. claims.source: Alcubierre 1994, Classical and Quantum Gravity vol. 11, opened and word-counted 2026-09-19
claims.text: ITS SOURCE DOCUMENT IS PEER-REVIEWED AND SAYS LESS THAN IS CLAIMED FOR IT. Reference 1 is Alcubierre, M., 'The warp drive: hyper-fast travel within general relativity', Classical and Quantum Gravity vol. 11, 1994. That paper states the requirement violates all three energy conditions, that energy density is everywhere negative, and that one needs exotic matter. Across the whole paper 'device' occurs 0 times and 'propulsion' once.

dossier.narrative:
The warp drive occupies an unusual position in this subject. Unlike most claimed mechanisms it has a real, citable, peer-reviewed origin: Alcubierre's 1994 paper, which this document's reference 1 prints in full. So the question is never whether the physics exists in the literature. It is what the literature actually says.

Alcubierre says it requires matter that violates all three energy conditions, with energy density everywhere negative, and states in terms that one needs exotic matter. Over the whole paper the word 'device' appears zero times and 'propulsion' appears once. It is a general relativity result about what a metric would have to look like, not an engineering proposal.

This DIA document takes the next step and quantifies it, tabulating the negative energy required for a warp bubble at light speed on the order of -10^42 joules before the reduction it argues for. Its own summary is careful in the same way, describing the idea that a sufficiently advanced technology may acquire direct control over higher dimensions as a possibility being explored rather than a result obtained.

The board carries all of this so that the gap is visible in one place: the peer-reviewed source, the government's quantification of what it would cost, and the popular claim that it is being done. The first two agree with each other and neither supports the third.
openQuestions: The author, withheld under the same exemptions as the rest of the series.
Whether the reduction this paper argues for has been assessed anywhere in the open literature.
dossier.whatItIs: A Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled 'Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions', series 'Acquisition Threat Support', published 2 April 2010, from the same FY2009 DIA series, author withheld under the same two exemptions. Its reference 1 is Alcubierre's 1994 paper in Classical and Quantum Gravity, printed in full.
dossier.whyImplicated: It is the government's own treatment of metric engineering, and unlike almost everything else in this subject it **prints the requirement as a number**. Two tables give the negative energy required for a warp bubble, before and after the reduction the paper argues for. A number is checkable, and a board built on grading evidence should prefer the document that gives one.
